items.title: AMC Theaters Launches Its Own Film Distribution Company As Small Budget Movies Soar
items.description: AMC Theaters isn’t merely a destination for watching new film releases; it now helps make those releases happen.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
AMC Theaters isn’t merely a destination for watching new film releases; it now helps make those releases happen.

Launched on August 31, 2026, AMC has rolled out Leawood Films, its very own movie distribution label that aims to bring small or mid-sized flicks to the big screen that have been completely financed and finished.

Speaking in a press release, AMC Entertainment chairman and CEO Adam Aron cited moviegoers’ increasing appetites for independent films.

“Ultimately, moviegoers consistently demonstrate their appetite for a wide variety of theatrical content, and we believe there are more outstanding films that deserve the opportunity to find audiences on the big screen,” he said. “Through Leawood Films, we believe we can bring meaningful value to filmmakers whose movies might otherwise not get made, or which might not be taken to theatres.

“We can assure them the availability of movie theatre screens and attractive economics, as well as have them benefit from our relationships across the exhibition industry, our proven marketing capabilities, and our extensive experience connecting theatrical content with moviegoing audiences.”

This doesn’t come as a huge surprise; some of the biggest films of the year were created on comparatively measly budgets (Obsession, Backrooms), and YouTube star Markiplier’s independent horror flick Iron Lung had so much hype behind it that AMC Theaters, along with several other major cinema chains, picked it up to help the movie become one of biggest independent film releases of all time.

“Leawood Films is being created with a straightforward objective, given that substantial excess capacity exists in the movie theatre industry: to bring more movies to theaters. If we can take steps to ensure that a few extra movies come to theaters each year, it is gravy for AMC in the United States and Odeon in Europe, as well as for our fellow exhibitors,” Aron added.

Tangentially, it’s worth noting that Markiplier also approached YouTube with the idea of distributing independent films on its platform, making AMC the latest major entertainment company to take notes based on shifting audience demands.

As per reporting from Deadline, Leawood Films’ board of advisors is made up of former Warner Bros Group chairman and Toby Emmerich, former Walt Disney Studios marketing president Ricky Strauss and former Paramount distribution veteran Kyle Davies.

AMC says this venture is a “low-risk opportunity” with the potential to catapult the next big film into the limelight. Perhaps Nicole Kidman wasn’t wrong when she said AMC Theaters “make movies better.”

items.title: Gal Gadot Says James Gunn and Peter Safran Told Her Wonder Woman 3 Was Happening Before Its Messy Cancellation
items.description: Former DC movie star Gal Gadot has opened up about the confusion surrounding Wonder Woman 3, saying that, even though it "wasn't handled elegantly," it's "all good" between her, James Gunn, and Peter Safran.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Former DC movie star Gal Gadot has opened up about the confusion surrounding Wonder Woman 3, saying that, even though it "wasn't handled elegantly," it's "all good" between her, James Gunn, and Peter Safran.

The story of Wonder Woman 3 is a bit of a mess. Gadot's return was seemingly greenlit, canceled, greenlit again, and, finally, canceled in the early 2020s, with its supposed early days unfortunately weighed down by leadership changes behind the scenes as Gunn and Safran stepped in to take over the DC movie business.

One of the stranger updates during the kerfuffle saw the actress confirm the two superhero film execs had told her she would come back as Diana Prince for Wonder Woman 3 before it was reported that Gunn and Safran didn't have any plans for a third movie from director Patty Jenkins after all. It was a back-and-forth painful enough to watch from the outside, but it was probably even more grueling on the inside.

Gadot recalled the confusion during an interview with Happy, Sad, Confused. She again confirmed that Gunn and Safran assured her Wonder Woman 3 was happening, going as far as to say that there was never a clear moment when the project was formally canned.

"No, they told me the opposite," she answered when asked about the circumstances surrounding the cancellation. "They were like, 'We're going to develop it with you, [Wonder Woman 3], but I saw the way everybody else was handled, right?"

The "everybody else" she referred to involves the former DC movie universe, often called the DC Extended Universe. It comprised films led by Gadot as Wonder Woman, Jason Momoa as Aquaman, and Henry Cavill as Superman. Cavill, in particular, had it rough when Gunn and Safran laid the groundwork for the DCU, as he also officially announced he would reprise his role as Clark Kent in October 2022 just to U-turn two months later.

"The Henry situation was not handled elegantly, to say the least," Gadot added. "Same with Patty – was not handled elegantly. I feel like, you know, we're all adults and it's all good, and it's not even about them."

She continued, saying that Gunn, Safran, and the rest of DC Studios are going "to do what they believe in, and it's all good." She said she's grateful she had the opportunity to be Wonder Woman at all and sends her best to whoever plays the part of the Amazonian superhero next. That said, don't expect her to ever play the part again, even if Gunn and Safran come knocking at her door.

"For me to go and do, for example, another Wonder Woman, I'm not sure I would at this point in my life with four children and different schools, and all of that. To check out all of them for such a long period of time… It doesn't work with my life anymore at this point."

For now, Wonder Woman 3 isn't happening, and it's unclear when the character will make her entrance into the DCU. Next up are movies like Clayface and Man of Tomorrow. Lanterns, one of the comic book movie universe's TV shows, is in the midst of its first season, with The People v. Gorilla Grodd confirmed to be in development. You can see the full breakdown for everything coming to the DCU here.

items.title: PlayStation Is Set to Pay Out $7.85 Million to Users as Part of Class-Action Lawsuit
items.description: PlayStation users may be eligible for a cut of a $7.85 million class-action lawsuit settlement very soon.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
PlayStation users may be eligible for a cut of a $7.85 million class-action lawsuit settlement very soon.

The class-action lawsuit, Caccuri v. Sony Interactive Entertainment, alleged that Sony violated anti-trust laws by forcing "consumers to pay more for certain digital games than they otherwise would have paid on the PlayStation Store.” It did so by removing digital vouchers for games from third-party retailers like Amazon or key resellers, meaning if you want a digital copy of a PlayStation game, you must buy it directly from the PlayStation Store.

This move removed the freedom of choice for a lot of players and has only become a hotter topic in recent months, as PlayStation plans to exit the physical media market in 2028. The lawsuit alleges that this decision pushed customers into paying more for games through the PlayStation Store.

Sony denied any wrongdoing and pushed back against claims that members were damaged by its actions. The court also hasn't decided if the company actually violated any laws yet, but it has preliminarily approved a $7.85 million settlement, subject to a final approval hearing on October 15. That hearing will decide how the funds will be distributed, lock in the final sum, and pay out attorney fees. For further updates, you can check out the official settlement website.

To be eligible for a cut of this settlement, you'll need to be a United States citizen who purchased a game from this list between April 1, 2019 and December 31, 2023. If you are elligible, PlayStation will deposit funds into your PSN account at a later date. If you deactivated your PSN, you can request a cash payment by submitting your qualifying purchase history to this email address: info@PSNDigitalGamesSettlement.com. It's unclear if you can request a cash payment with an existing PSN account, but if you can, PlayStation users can view their purchase history directly through their account on PlayStation's website if needed.

As is the case with class-action lawsuits, we won't know how much money individuals will get until it starts going out. It could be a few bucks, it could be dozens of dollars. Either way, free money is free money.

In related news, a separate lawsuit has seen PlayStation admitting that players don't own their digital games. This may not come as a shock to some, since the terms of service often use the term "license" in relation to digital games, but it is messy optics as the company tries to navigate backlash from its pivot to an all-digital future.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: 'Take My Money Now' — Viral Game Lets Your Giant Pet Cat Join You in Combat, and Players Can't Wait
items.description: An indie game where players share heartbeats with their pet cat, which can transform into a giant kitty big enough to ride on and defeat enemies, is going viral — and it’s not hard to see why.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
An indie game where players share heartbeats with their pet cat, which can transform into a giant kitty big enough to ride on and defeat enemies, is going viral — and it’s not hard to see why.

The game, titled Ylem’s Cat, is the debut offering of a small, independent studio based in Guangzhou, China. It was first revealed at gamescom this year, and it’s already sweeping across social media.

Per its listing on Steam, the game’s official logline is as follows: “Ylem’s Cat is an action-adventure game driven by the bond between a girl and her cat. Led by curiosity and knowledge, Molly sets out on a journey to find her missing mother across a dying planet, exploring ruins and uncovering the truth buried within the giants.”

While the game’s graphics are truly stunning and its gameplay loop seems immersive enough, the cat is the real selling point here. It can join you in combat and bop enemies on the head, and you can even use the reflection from your bow to play with it like a laser pointer. The feline’s realistic behavior will no doubt be a selling point for cat lovers (but we have to warn you that it does seem like it falls into mortal peril at one point in the trailer).

The game follows Molly in the wake of a terrible disaster after a mysterious cat saves her life. The cat — which she names Mio, after its meow — now shares a heartbeat with Molly, and it’s being hunted by robotic beings named Sentinels.

Mio helps you both in combat and in exploration, and can grow bigger or smaller depending on the task at hand. “In combat, the more you learn to fight together, the easier it becomes,” the game’s Steam page reads. “In exploration, keep an eye on Mio — the little cat has its own curiosities, and those might matter more than you think.”

New game announced where your cat companion has its own mood swings

- You share the same heartbeat
- You name it Mio after the sound it makes
- The Sentinels are hunting your cat
- It grows giant and you can ride it

Game is Ylem's Cat pic.twitter.com/9x1FnjIiGv

— Indie Game Joe (@IndieGameJoe) August 29, 2026

Thus far, Ylem’s Cat has no release date, but developers are reportedly heading toward an eventual 2028 launch. Players are already impatiently waiting to get their hands on the game, with some making comparisons to the realistic animal behavior of Trico from The Last Guardian.

“Just imagine a cat of that size getting the zoomies,” one remarked.

“Bro, take my money now!” another said.

“Knowing my cat's mood swings, I would PROBABLY be murdered if it was that size,” yet another joked.

Just imagine a cat of this size getting the zoomies 🤣 pic.twitter.com/DcgEGbDA2C

— Monastery - Wishlist on Steam (@Unseen_Domains) August 31, 2026

Just like Toriko... So cute! pic.twitter.com/TvdPBTi6nQ

— Locke (@Locke3522) August 30, 2026

BRO TAKE MY MONEY NOW pic.twitter.com/as2JSdF2bK

— NinjaGato (@ninjagato465) August 30, 2026

This is the latest pet-focused action game to turn heads after Stray Dog: nobody cares went viral earlier this month. The Souslike title follows a stray dog searching for its captured master in a world overrun with danger, using a sword in its jaws to defeat foes standing in its way.

items.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Developers Address Time to Kill Criticisms and Tweak Weapons in New Beta Update
items.description: Infinity Ward has addressed the state of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's time to kill and tweaked a handful of weapons in a new beta update.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Infinity Ward has addressed the state of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's time to kill and tweaked a handful of weapons in a new beta update.

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's beta is coming to a close, but Infinity Ward is still updating the hell out of it. The latest update was pushed this morning before the beta officially winds down tomorrow. Per the patch notes, a bunch of weapons have been tuned following feedback from fans, including the ISO Nightshade SMG, which got a slight buff with damage improvements. The PPSH, Krait P68, Han 86, and Hyeon Burst all got various buffs as well, with the latter's headshot damage multiplier increasing from 1 to 1.1.

A handful of weapons got nerfed, but the most notable hit was taken by the M4 Hurricane variant, which had its damage decreased. Infinity Ward also used the update as an opportunity to address the game's time to kill, which was divisive in the first beta weekend for being far too fast. Following some adjustments, MW4's TTK is more in line with where Infinity Ward wants it to be.

"Over the weekend, we've been reviewing your gameplay and feedback carefully," said the studio. "We feel that TTK on average is much closer to where we wanted it to be after Weekend 1, but there's always room to refine individual weapons to make sure they're balanced across the board. These changes provide tuning for each class to do well at its role."

Being responsive to feedback is a big part of Infinity Ward's mission this year. Fans were frustrated with Modern Warfare 2 (2022) because it felt like Infinity Ward ignored or brushed off critiques about major aspects such as gameplay pacing, mini-map functionality, and SBMM. With Modern Warfare 4, Infinity Ward is trying to be more receptive.

"I think in MW2, we definitely didn't communicate as well as we should have," said Studio Multiplayer Creative Director Joe Cecot in an exclusive interview with IGN. "I think we've remedied that in crazy ways with this project. Even with the amount of stuff that I get sent to my desk to review like, "Hey, we want to respond to this." And then I review copy or I'm writing something, it's a huge shift. That's going to continue into live support and I think you see it at our studio head level. [Infinity Ward co-studio head] Mark Grigsby is posting, the Infinity Word account is posting, the Call of Duty account is posting, and they're all in unison posting. They're not separate from each other. I think it's really powerful and it feels really good to us."

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: GTA 6 Gets Even More New Screenshots as Rockstar Locks in for November Launch
items.description: It seems the drought of Grand Theft Auto 6 news has finally come to an end, as Rockstar has published even more screenshots for fans to comb through.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
It seems the drought of Grand Theft Auto 6 news has finally come to an end, as Rockstar has published even more screenshots for fans to comb through.

It seems the floodgates for GTA 6's summer marketing campaign have finally opened after last week's extended look gameplay premiere. Today, instead of video for Jason and Lucia's story, Rockstar has published a nice selection of fresh screenshots, revealing new options for character customization, potential story moments, and a closer look at Vice City.

Rockstar has an entire page on its website dedicated to new GTA 6 screenshots that range from pictures of in-progress robberies and explosive cars to muddin' parties and romantic nights out on the town. Of the 99 images available, at least three have never been seen before, and many of the others are only now getting high-quality releases. You can see the three new GTA 6 screenshots, as well as some of the other images Rockstar shared, below.

Grand Theft Auto fans are still parsing through all of the content themselves, but three images in particular seem to be brand new and have fans especially worked up: one of Jason and Lucia in a car, a real-life Miami condo recreated in Vice City, and a menacing shot of the two protagonists as they looked down on someone they maybe, probably just murdered. It's a lot to go through, so let's start with that first one.

Players will probably spend a lot of time in GTA 6, so it's nice to know there will be what seems to be a shopping mall's worth of customization items to dress up Jason and Lucia. The first image puts that on full display, showing the latter criminal decked out with piercings, tattoos, and bangs. Jason, meanwhile, looks almost like a different person thanks to his slick-backed do and facial hair.

items.title: RIP to Disney+'s Live-Action Gargoyles Reboot
items.description: Gargoyles' creator Greg Weisman has revealed that the live-action adaptation of the '90s cartoon series is no longer moving forward.
items.author: Rachel Weber
items.content:
Gargoyles creator Greg Weisman has revealed that the live-action adaptation of the '90s cartoon series is no longer moving forward. The show had been planned as a Disney+ release, with James Wan's production company, Atomic Monster, leading the project.

"Well, I know the live-action side of it is, uh, the Atomic Monster had the license to develop a live-action Gargoyles for Disney+, and that’s dead," he told ComicsOnline. "I have no idea about animation, but there are no current plans for live-action."

The show first aired in 1994 and centered on a bunch of (you guessed it) Gargoyles, who turn to stone in daylight hours and find themselves in a modern-day New York City, becoming its defenders. The iconic Keith David played the leader of the petrifying pack, Goliath, and his clone, Thailog.

The live-action reboot was announced in 2023 with Annabelle and The Nun writer Gary Dauberman as showrunner, writer, and executive producer. Last year, Dauberman told Collider that the original cartoon "lends itself to a really cool live-action version," and said his take would be "still keeping that darkness to it."

If the news is hard to hear, you can still stream all three seasons of the original Gargoyles animated version on Disney+. In a 2021 IGN retrospective, our writer argued the show "helped to redefine cartoon villainy in the ’90s."

items.title: Lion King Lyricist Ordered to Pay Nearly $40,000 to Cover Comedian's Attorney Fees After Suing Him Over Joke Translation of 'Circle of Life' Lyrics
items.description: The Grammy-winning lyricist behind The Lion King’s famous opening vocals is now being ordered to pay nearly $40,000 in attorneys’ fees after unsuccessfully suing a comedian for poking fun at the song.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
The Grammy-winning lyricist behind The Lion King’s famous opening vocals is now being ordered to pay nearly $40,000 in attorneys’ fees after unsuccessfully suing a comedian for poking fun at the song.

South African comedian Learnmore Mwanyenyeka, better known by his alias Jonasi, was hit with a $27 million lawsuit in March 2026 from plaintiff Lebohang Morake, who penned the Zulu lyrics that are sung at the beginning of "The Circle of Life" in Disney’s animated animal epic.

Jonasi made the joke during an episode of the One54 Africa podcast in February, where he playfully translated the line as, “Look, there is a lion! Oh my god.” While it got a laugh from the show’s hosts at the time, the song’s lyricist didn’t find it very funny.

A March 16 lawsuit filed in the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California labeled Jonasi’s humorous mistranslation as a “fabricated, trivializing distortion meant as a sick joke,” saying it damaged the “royal praise poetry” written by Morake that "stands independently as an African vocal proclamation grounded in South African tradition” outside of its use in The Lion King.

For reference, Morake’s lawsuit translated the line “Nants’ingonyama bagithi Baba” as “All hail the king, we all bow in the presence of the king.” The suit mentioned that “ngonyama” can also translate to Lion in Zulu, but argued that the term “signifies kingship” due to Praise Imbongi tradition and the use of royal metaphor, per NBC News.

In a now-deleted Instagram post, Jonasi said that he and Morake spoke about the situation privately. "This was just a joke, and comedy always has a way of starting a conversation,” he said. “I told him this. This is now your chance to actually educate people because now people are listening. I was even ready to create a video with him, to be honest. Personally, I had no idea it had a deeper meaning."

Jonasi was famously served a lawsuit over the joke during a live performance that same month. Now, five months later, the suit has been struck down, with Morake ordered to pay thousands of dollars to cover Jonasi’s attorney fees.

More specifically, he’ll have to shell out $39,560, as laid out in a court order filed on August 28, 2026. The order says the “prevailing defendant” ultimately won the case due to an Anti-SLAPP motion, which basically means the court struck down what it believed was a frivolous and costly suit designed to punish Jonasi for his joke.

The suit was officially dismissed on July 10, 2026. Speaking with the Rolling Stone, Jonasi’s lawyer, Bryan Sullivan, celebrated the ruling as a win for free speech.

“We have always believed this was a frivolous lawsuit in violation of our client’s First Amendment rights,” he told the outlet.

items.title: 'It Ended My Old Life'  — DayZ Felt Like Dying, Says Creator
items.description: Dean Hall, creator of zombie survival game DayZ and founder of RocketWerkz, seems to have a complicated relationship with his biggest hit, which was first released as a mod for Arma 2 in 2012.
items.author: Rachel Weber
items.content:
Dean Hall, creator of zombie survival game DayZ and founder of RocketWerkz, seems to have a complicated relationship with his biggest hit, which was first released as a mod for Arma 2 in 2012.

"When DayZ happened, it was like dying," Hall told PC Gamer. "It ended my old life. My relationship with everyone who I knew up to that point changed completely."

"It was obviously an amazing thing that happened to me," he added. "I loved making the mod, and I loved that feeling, and I've been chasing it ever since."

The game started life as a mod for Arma 2 and its expansion pack Operation Arrowhead and was so popular with gamers that just a few months later Hall announced that Arma 2 developer Bohemia Interactive was creating a standalone version of the game, with Hall as project lead.

"People think I'm a game developer who came up from [being] a modder, and I would say I'm a modder who makes games during the day," Hall added. "I was born a modder, and I will die a modder. And I think if there's a lesson out there for any aspiring game devs, I think it's mod games. You will learn even faster than making them."

In February 2014 Hall stepped down from the project lead role and went on to start his own studio, RocketWerkz. Its releases since include VR strategy game Out Of Ammo and space survival sim Icarus and is currently working on Kitten Space Agency. As well as being a spaceflight sim, the game is a proof of concept for Hall's contribution-based development model.

"With Kitten Space Agency, the game is completely free," he said. "It's funded entirely by contributions. So that really puts it in front of the gamer's face. If you want this game to exist, how much is it worth? Because it's all on you."

items.title: Fans Can't Decide if Hideo Kojima Actually Liked Ridley Scott's The Dog Stars
items.description: Kojima’s brief review for Ridley Scott’s latest movie betrays how he really feels about the divisive post-apocalyptic flick… At least, that’s what fans are saying.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Hideo Kojima’s brief review for Ridley Scott’s The Dog Stars betrays how he really feels about the divisive post-apocalyptic movie… At least, that’s what fans are saying.

Scott’s latest movie hasn’t exactly been well-received. The movie was a box office bomb, earning just $19 million during its global opening. Critics’ opinions have been similarly brutal, with IGN’s Leanne Butkovic scoring the film a 5 out of 10, calling it a "post-apocalyptic survival story that’s encased in three layers of emotionally protective bubble wrap with a wild third-act twist."

Fans believe Kojima, an acclaimed video game director and film connoisseur, feels much the same way, owing to a trend they’ve observed in his social media posts discussing movies he’s recently watched. If you’re familiar with Kojima’s online presence, you’ll know that the man isn’t very fussed about public perception (some of his retweets are straight up WILD), but when it comes to expressing his dislike for films, fans claim that he often doesn’t say anything of substance at all.

Usually, when Kojima likes a movie, he’ll create a lengthy post diving into everything he admired about it, as seen in the high praise he gave to Kane Parson’s Backrooms. However, for The Dog Stars, he merely remarked on what he initially expected from the film… and that’s about it.

"Peter Heller's original novel, The Dog Stars (previously published in Japanese under the title Itsuka Boku ga Kaeru Basho / The Place I'll Return to Someday), has been sitting on my bookshelf for years, unread. Since it's literary fiction rather than science fiction, I went to see the movie, picturing it might be something along the lines of Cormac McCarthy's The Road. The music was by Harry. They weren't selling (didn’t make) a pamphlet for the film," he said on his English X account.

It was a strikingly bland post in comparison to his other, far more colorful reviews of films he distinctly loves — and because of this, fans are convinced that Kojima, much like other reviewers, wasn't its biggest fan. Though of course, we can’t outright say that, given he didn’t say as much in his post.

Peter Heller's original novel, “The Dog Stars” (previously published in Japanese under the title Itsuka Boku ga Kaeru Basho / The Place I'll Return to Someday), has been sitting on my bookshelf for years, unread. Since it's literary fiction rather than science fiction, I went to… pic.twitter.com/irC8ZjoMrH

— HIDEO_KOJIMA (@HIDEO_KOJIMA_EN) August 30, 2026

"You can tell he didn’t like it because he said nothing about the actual film, lol," one user said in the comments.

"He said nothing about the film so he hated it lmao," another joked.

"Ridley's a genius, he created a genre of Kojima tweets. Saying nothing about the actual film while talking about it," yet another said.

Scott’s name has been all over social media as of late, in part due to The Dog Stars as well as several interviews he’s given to the press. In one of these interviews, Scott confirmed that he is developing a sequel to Alien: Covenant with Michael Fassbender, partly because he believes the Alien franchise he created "needs some help," as he felt Alien: Romulus was just "OK."

items.title: Sony CEO Explains Why It Isn’t 'Aggressively Marketing' the PlayStation 5 Anymore
items.description: Sony CEO Hiroki Totoki confirmed that the company is no longer “aggressively marketing” the PlayStation 5, saying it’s not necessary now that the console is in the later stages of its life cycle.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Sony CEO Hiroki Totoki confirmed that the company is no longer “aggressively marketing” the PlayStation 5, saying it’s not necessary now that the console is in the later stages of its life cycle.

It’s been nearly six years since the PlayStation 5 first released in November 2020. We’ve come a long way from the days of scalpers making purchases nearly impossible; but these consoles are now largely out of stock at several major retailers once again following Rockstar’s extended look at GTA 6 that released on Netflix this past Thursday.

This marks a sharp turn for the console after it experienced its lowest May sales in the PS5’s history after Sony announced price hikes across all versions of the hardware in April 2026. While highly-anticipated games like GTA 6 seem to be doing all the marketing on Sony’s behalf right now, the company has confirmed that it isn’t fussed about advertising the PlayStation 5 these days.

Hiroki Totoki, CEO at Sony, explained this strategy during an interview with the Wall Street Journal in mid-August, where he admitted that the business’s current goal is profiting off of its existing PlayStation Plus userbase as much as possible.

“We are in the latter half of the life cycle for a PlayStation console,” he said. “That means that we do not need to ‘aggressively sell’ the console today. And rather than that, we’re focusing on recurring revenue from the recurrent userbase. And already, PlayStation Plus has more than 125 million monthly active users today, and how to monetize from those users is quite important for us.”

As expected, comments beneath the video are making sure to point out the company’s future plans to end the production of physical game discs starting January 2028, with one writing on YouTube, “Bring back ‘Only on PlayStation,’ keep physical media.”

“They’ll regret terminating physical media,” another said.

“Maybe they can revert and bring back physical discs, for starters,” another wrote.

These comments are the same under any major post discussing PlayStation, or even posts from the brand, itself. Advertisements for film adaptations of popular games on its consoles are facing a similar fate as players inundate the comments section protesting Sony’s plans for an all-digital future — a future that’s looking increasingly bleak, based on the company’s recent statements to disgruntled customers.

In July, Sony’s chief financial officer, Lin Tao, confirmed that it will "cautiously move forward" with killing off physical discs, arguing that this decision was made in response to the increasing “digitization of contents.”

And on August 21, Sony responded to a class action lawsuit from consumers who argued that the PlayStation digital store doesn’t make it obvious that players are merely purchasing a revocable license, instead of fully owning the games permanently.

“In the digital age, it is not plausible to allege that reasonable consumers believed they were obtaining ‘ownership’ of a digital game,” the company said.

Thus far, the future of the PlayStation 6 is unknown, but players are worried that both this console and Xbox's Project Helix will be digital-only by default.

It’s been nearly six years since the PlayStation 5 first released in November 2020. We’ve come a long way from the days of scalpers making purchases nearly impossible; but these consoles are now largely out of stock at several major retailers once again following Rockstar’s extended look at GTA 6 that released on Netflix this past Thursday.

This marks a sharp turn for the console after it experienced its lowest May sales in the PS5’s history after Sony announced price hikes across all versions of the hardware in April 2026. While highly-anticipated games like GTA 6 seem to be doing all the marketing on Sony’s behalf right now, the company has confirmed that it isn’t fussed about advertising the PlayStation 5 these days.

Hiroki Totoki, CEO at Sony, explained this strategy during an interview with the Wall Street Journal in mid-August, where he admitted that the business’s current goal is profiting off of its existing PlayStation Plus userbase as much as possible.

“We are in the latter half of the life cycle for a PlayStation console,” he said. “That means that we do not need to ‘aggressively sell’ the console today. And rather than that, we’re focusing on recurring revenue from the recurrent userbase. And already, PlayStation Plus has more than 125 million monthly active users today, and how to monetize from those users is quite important for us.”

As expected, comments beneath the video are making sure to point out the company’s future plans to end the production of physical game discs starting January 2028, with one writing on YouTube, “Bring back ‘Only on PlayStation,’ keep physical media.”

“They’ll regret terminating physical media,” another said.

“Maybe they can revert and bring back physical discs, for starters,” another wrote.

These comments are the same under any major post discussing PlayStation, or even posts from the brand, itself. Advertisements for film adaptations of popular games on its consoles are facing a similar fate as players inundate the comments section protesting Sony’s plans for an all-digital future — a future that’s looking increasingly bleak, based on the company’s recent statements to disgruntled customers.

“In the digital age, it is not plausible to allege that reasonable consumers believed they were obtaining ‘ownership’ of a digital game,” the company said.

items.title: Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered Dev Says GTA 6 Was 'Never Part of Our Thinking' When Choosing a Release Date
items.description: Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered will take on GTA 6 when both games launch this November, but the team behind the arena fighter said Rockstar's latest was "never part of our thinking" when choosing a release date.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered will take on Grand Theft Auto 6 when both games launch this November, but the team behind the arena fighter said Rockstar's latest title was "never part of our thinking" when choosing a release date.

In case you haven't heard, GTA 6 comes out November 19, a choice that prompted a wave of other publishers to do everything they can to not launch their games anywhere near that date. The belief is the fallout from a game 13 years in the making will consume the weeks before and after its release, but Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered has emerged as one of the very, very few titles willing to brave the storm.

GTA 6 is indeed primed for an explosive launch, but the team at developer Pipeworks and publisher Atari haven't seemed too worried about how this could affect the remaster for a 2000s classic. In fact, after revealing their November 3 release date, the internet rallied behind the kaiju fighting game, filling feeds with memes as the King of the Monsters (and the upcoming Barbie Rewind) stomped forward.

As part of a sweeping interview about the new remaster, IGN asked longtime Pipeworks developer and senior designer Simon Strange about how the release date for Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered was chosen and how GTA 6 played a factor in that decision. You might be surprised to hear Rockstar's return to Vice City wasn't really on their radar.

"I have also loved all those memes. I think that's great. Honestly, wasn't even in our heads at all when we were picking the release date," Strange said when asked about how the date was picked. "That's not my business. I make the video games. I'm not too worried about when they come out. If Atari had come to us and said, 'Wow, we can't because we think it's going to affect the sales with GTA,' we would've had that discussion. But no one ever said anything."

https://t.co/Lh4c0SyWvl pic.twitter.com/4hzmDYUVVy

— 🐙Dumbo Octopus🐙 (@DumboOctopus4) June 7, 2026

Strange made a good point: November 3 is Godzilla's birthday. The original film released on that day in 1954, it's when IP owner Toho recognizes as 'Godzilla Day,' and this year, regardless of whatever is going on with GTA 6, it's when Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered is coming to PC and consoles.

Strange clarified that making sure Gojira kept his November birthday was simply a matter of respect. After Pipeworks landed its contract with Atari and pinned a timeline for physical disc manufacturing, the date was locked in.

"So, the GTA thing, that's hilarious," Strange continued. "It's a really cute meme. We've all really enjoyed that. It was never part of our thinking. I wasn't looking at that calendar and being worried in any way, or thinking about what other games are coming out because the Godzilla fans are very excited for it. They'd buy it on any day that it came out, and putting it on Godzilla's birthday, that's just respectful."

Atari admitted it was "certainly aware of the proximity" to the release of GTA 6 when running the numbers tied to its release date. Though still in November, the publisher felt the break between releases gave Godzilla – and Barbie – more than enough room to breathe.

"There were a number of factors at play that led to the selection of November 12 as the release date for Barbie Rewind," an Atari spokesperson told IGN. "In the end, it made the most sense in our calendar, and we felt the cozy/retro vibe of Rewind and the Barbie brand was going to pull in its own, discrete audience.

"It has been exciting to see fans' reactions to the idea of our two games, Godzilla: DAMM Remastered and Barbie Rewind, releasing in November with GTA. The amount and quality of creative content fans are posting online is astounding and a joy to watch. They have made the proximity of the releases a fun event."

GTA 6 or not, Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered will launch for PC via Steam, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S November 3. Barbie Rewind will follow November 12, 2026, for PC via Steam, Switch and Switch 2, PS4, PS5, Xbox One, and Xbox Series X/S. Pipeworks is also scheduled to release a PC demo for its Godzilla game October 15.

We'll have more to share from our talk with Pipeworks soon, so be sure to keep an eye out for the full interview. In the meantime, don't forget to check out our preview.

items.title: PlayStation Claims Digital Games Are Not Really Owned by Players in Response to Class-Action Lawsuit
items.description: Sony has given a divisive response to a class-action lawsuit that argues the PlayStation online store doesn’t make it obvious enough that players are merely purchasing a revocable license to play a game, and not the game itself.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Sony has given a divisive response to a class-action lawsuit that argues the PlayStation online store doesn’t make it obvious enough that players are merely purchasing a revocable license to play a game, rather than owning the entire game itself.

The lawsuit, filed on June 18, 2026, says PlayStation “fails to clearly and conspicuously disclose to consumers at the point of sale that these transactions do not convey ownership of the digital games.” It argues that the company “relegates this information to inconspicuous text or separate agreements that consumers are not required to affirmatively acknowledge.”

This, at least, is true; before checking out on PlayStation’s digital storefront, a message is displayed in small text that reads: "By selecting [Confirm Purchase], you agree to complete the purchase in accordance with the PlayStation Terms of Service before using this content. You further acknowledge that your purchase of this digital product amounts to a license subject to the Software Product License Agreement.”

PlayStation has now provided its retort to this lawsuit. In an August 21 filing in California’s Northern District Court, it argues that it has done enough to make it obvious that customers are simply buying a license, rather than the full game for their permanent ownership.

“As Plaintiffs admit, Section 1 of the SPLA likewise explains that ‘The Software is licensed to you, not sold.’ This makes sense. In the digital age, it is not plausible to allege that reasonable consumers believed they were obtaining ‘ownership’ of a digital game. Were that the case, then Plaintiff Edward Heycock would not have been able to obtain the game Resident Evil Requiem on February 25, 2026 for $69.99 from the PlayStation Store after Plaintiff Jason Mendoza had obtained Resident Evil Requiem on February 14, 2026, because Mr. Mendoza, not Sony, would have owned it then," the company's response reads.

Needless to say, this reply has sparked a fierce wave of backlash from players on social media, who are already riled up over Sony’s decision to end the production of physical game discs starting January 2028. With this context in mind, many feel Sony’s counterargument is downright malicious: If the company continues to pursue an all-digital future, then players will truly own nothing outright, as the game licenses on Sony’s digital storefront can simply be yanked away at any time.

“‘The Software is licensed to you, not sold.’ Then why does the page say I'm ‘Buying’ it? Sounds like false advertisement to me,” one wrote on X.

“They can't simply take away your full game if you have the full file installed and it’s working and complete without the need of servers, and also can't make unaccessible or unplayable for no reason,” another argued.

“The United States needs to pass a law to catch up with the era of digital media. I should be able to own what is sold to me, and I should be able to do whatever I want to do with what I own,” another urged.

If “license” is being used as the legal mechanism that transforms an ordinary purchase into a restricted permission, shouldn't the law define what a consumer license actually is, rather than allowing every publisher to construct its own version and then rely on the same word to…

— aCat (@Alex1Ne0) August 29, 2026

“The Software is licensed to you, not sold.”

Then why does the page says I'm "Buying" it? sounds like false advertisement to me. pic.twitter.com/bvIz5J4iy9

— Backlog Dragon - Gaming VTuber (@BacklogDragon) August 29, 2026

If a company sells you a digital license, it must guarantee permanent access to a downloadable copy of the licensed product

If the company shuts down, abandons the product, or goes bankrupt, the game must automatically be transferred to an independent digital archive, together…

— Rage Crusader (@RageCrusader) August 29, 2026

This argument is at the heart of another lawsuit the company is facing in Mexico. Brought forward in July, Mexican lawmakers allege that PlayStation is engaging in “anti-competitive practices” by choosing to end physical disc production, as it would severely limit competition from independent games retailers by forcing players to go through its digital storefront if they want to play PlayStation games.

PlayStation's online store is central to another lawsuit in the Netherlands, where Dutch Consumer Group Stichting Massaschade & Consument argues that its customers are getting charged more for digital games in comparison to customers in different countries.

Sony, for its part, has made no move to renege on its choice to kill physical games. In July, the company's chief financial officer, Lin Tao, said it will "cautiously move this forward" with this plan, claiming that it is keeping players' high emotions around the topic in "consideration."

"In the future digital ecosystem, how do we engage the gamers is something that we would like to continue to explore," she said.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

items.title: GTA 6's Relationship Mechanic Is 'Cheating' on Your Real-Life Partner and Break Up Worthy, According to Angry Spouses
items.description: A bunch of angry spouses on social media believe that Grand Theft Auto 6's in-depth relationship mechanic is equivalent to cheating on your real life partner and worth breaking up over.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
A swath of angry spouses on social media believe that Grand Theft Auto 6's in-depth relationship mechanic is equivalent to cheating on your real-life partner and worth breaking up over.

Last week, we got a boatload of details on Grand Theft Auto 6 thanks to media previews and an extended look at the game from Rockstar itself. One of the big takeaways from this media blitz is that there is an actual relationship between the game's two protagonists, Jason and Lucia, that players can nurture. You can take the other character on dates, do crimes together, text them, and even hold hands (aw!). For some people, though, that last detail causing tensions in their real life relationships.

Over on TikTok, a variety of concerned partners stated that wouldn't allow their partner to play the game, and a concerning amount of comments on these posts echoed this sentiment.

"In absolutely no human way is my fiancé playing GTA 6," said one TikToker. "You literally have to maintain a relationship with a girl [in] the video game and text her, and she'll get mad if you don't text her back. You have to take her on dates and you can have [sex] with her. [...] Don't let your boyfriend or fiancé or husband play GTA 6."

Other TikTok creators outright labeled playing the game as cheating.

@el.michelle3

The whole relationship and yk what else

♬ life goes on - lucie

This has become a major subject of discourse on social media since the GTA 6 extended look went live on August 27. Some are pushing back on the idea, arguing that it's simply a video game and not that deep. Others have also pointed out that millions of people have played The Sims for years, having virtual sex and creating entire families without anyone raising an eyebrow.

Rockstar has also been very clear that you don't actually have to engage with this part of GTA 6 if you don't want to. The two characters want a relationship at the start of the game, but it's up to the player to actively pursue that. If you don't, they won't be as head-over-heels for each other, but will still have each other's backs when it matters most. If you do choose to make the two a power couple, you'll likely get more mileage out of the game, though.

"When you bring them together, it feels like you’re a steward of their relationship, and you feel protective of them as a unit," said Rockstar North co-studio head, Rob Nelson, in an exclusive interview with IGN. "But this is something we did not know when we started, and it really had to be something we felt our way through. But I will say that whether you’re getting in trouble, or you’re running from the cops, or getting in a car, or waiting for the other one — playing as them together feels very cool. It feels like you’re taking care of them, if that’s something you’re into."

Rockstar has yet to confirm if you can have sex with the two characters outside of scripted story moments. The trailers certainly imply there will be sexual scenes between the two, but whether you can actively initiate that by building the relationship meter is unclear. IGN broached the subject with Nelson, who noted that physical intimacy is a notable part of a relationship and that Rockstar is trying to figure out how to implement that side of things into the game in a way that feels right.

“For anybody that wants to play around with the idea of role playing their relationship, it's amazing," said Nelson. "So many people on the team have connected with the characters. But physical intimacy is a huge part of a relationship, and so it has to be done right. Like anything that we do, we have to iterate and try things and iterate on it until we figure out what feels right."

GTA 4 allowed you to develop relationships which would lead to Niko being invited for intercourse, but it was never explicitly shown. On a more controversal note, Rockstar Games developed an interactive sex mini-game in 2005's Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. It was eventually cut from the game to avoid an Adults Only rating, which would've prevented Rockstar from being able to sell the game at most major retailers. However, the files remained in the game and modders were able to add it back in. This led to major issues for Rockstar, including legal battles, a recall of existing copies of the game, and scrutiny from the government. As a result, you probably shouldn't expect any interactive sex mini-games in GTA 6.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: Shailene Woodley Reflects on Cut Mary Jane Role in The Amazing Spider-Man 2
items.description: Actress Shailene Woodley reflects on playing Mary Jane Watson in The Amazing Spider-Man 2 before her scenes were cut from the final film.
items.author: Jim Vejvoda
items.content:
You may recall that Shailene Woodley was cast as Mary Jane Watson in The Amazing Spider-Man 2. The Divergent and Big Little Lies actor shot her scenes opposite Andrew Garfield’s wall-crawler for what she now calls her “dream” role in the Marvel-Sony sequel, only to later find out she had been cut from the movie entirely before it hit theaters in 2014.

In a recent chat with the SAG-AFTRA Foundation’s Conversations (via The Hollywood Reporter), Woodley recalled her disappointment when she learned a year after she’d shot her scenes that she had been cut from Amazing Spider-Man 2.

“I was cast as Mary Jane for Spider-Man, which was my dream. Oh my god, Spider-Man’s my favorite superhero; Mary Jane was my favorite character growing up. So, when I got it, I was like, ‘This is so exciting!'” Woodley said.

“We filmed like three scenes together, me and Andrew Garfield. And then, like a year later, they were like, ‘So, you’re not in the movie anymore.’ And I was like, ‘What? So, there was no reintroduction,” Woodley said. “That’s what I was told, but again, who knows what the truth is? I could have been terrible, and they were like, ‘We can’t do this.'”

The Amazing Spider-Man 2 ends with the death of Emma Stone’s Gwen Stacy, and the filmmakers said at the time that was one reason they cut Woodley’s Mary Jane from the movie.

“Shailene is a brilliant actress, and she did a great couple days of work,” director Marc Webb said. “But it was very difficult to introduce someone as a competing love interest when so much is on the table with Peter and Gwen.”

items.title: Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet Has Finished Shooting Its Performance Capture, Confirms Naughty Dog
items.description: Naughty Dog's next game, Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, has wrapped shooting on the game's performance capture.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Naughty Dog's next game, Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, has wrapped shooting its performance capture.

Naughty Dog confirmed in a new social media post that Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet has concluded its "cinematic shoot." This means that all of the story content has been captured by the actors and likely suggests that the game is entering its final stages. Performance capture often takes years, with actors performing the game in chunks as the team simultaneously continues to create the game.

"See you, space cowboy..."
That is a wrap on the very ambitious Intergalactic cinematic shoot! This cast killed it! Cannot wait to show you their incredible work when the time is right! pic.twitter.com/WgqgcHGm8K

— Naughty Dog (@Naughty_Dog) August 31, 2026

For reference, The Last of Us Part 2 wrapped performance capture in April 2019, roughly a year before the game's release in June 2020. However, Naughty Dog had initially planned for that game to release in February 2020 before a delay pushed it to May 2020. Once COVID happened, the game was briefly delayed once more to June 2020.

With that said, it's possible that Intergalactic is just a year away from launch. A 2027 release has been rumored and speculated for a while, but nothing has been confirmed by Naughty Dog. There is a PlayStation State of Play later this week, so it's possible that Naughty Dog will share new details on the game there. It has been nearly two years since the title was announced, and Naughty Dog hasn't said much about it since its reveal.

Fans have also been frustrated that Naughty Dog hasn't had a game since 2020, but that was never part of the plan. The studio was meant to release The Last of Us Online between The Last of Us 2 and Intergalactic, but its cancellation created a more significant gap in releases for the studio. Going forward, there likely won't be big generational gaps as Naughty Dog has multiple projects in development, which are speculated to be Uncharted 5 and The Last of Us Part 3.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: Sony Reveals Live TV on PS5, Free With Ads Starting Today
items.description: Sony has revealed Live TV on PS5, bringing television free with ads to PlayStation users in the U.S. starting later today.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Sony has revealed Live TV on PS5, bringing television free with ads to PlayStation users in the U.S. starting later today.

It's an unexpected announcement for the gaming company that was outlined in a PlayStation.Blog post today. Described as a "free ad-supported experience from Sony Pictures Television," Live TV on PS5 supports more than 100 live channels and what the company promises to be a "growing selection of on-demand entertainment including news, sports, movies, TV shows, anime and more."

Players will be able to access the new live TV feature on their PlayStation 5 devices at an unspecified point later today. According to Sony, all you have to do is navigate to the console's Media tab, select "Live TV on PS5" while signed into a PlayStation Network account, and voila! You can see a 30-second introduction video for the surprise feature below.

Sony did a much better job of detailing the specific entertainment PS5 owners can take advantage of with a full breakdown on its site. You can see everything you need to know below.

  • Movies – Free movies across action, horror, sci-fi and more, with channels including MovieSphere by Lionsgate, 50 Cent Action, FilmRise Free Movies, Sony One Horror Hits and Cinevault.
  • TV Shows – Fan-favorite programming including Community, The Shield, Hell’s Kitchen, The Walking Dead, Forensic Files, Unsolved Mysteries, Deal or No Deal USA and Fear Factor, plus Ice Road Truckers from A+E’s HISTORY.
  • Anime – Anime favorites including Naruto, Sailor Moon, Hunter x Hunter, Death Note and more, including exclusive channels Black Clover and Box Sets channels from Crunchyroll.
  • Sports – Sports programming from FOX Sports, NASCAR, NBC Sports Now, UFC and more spanning MMA, football, hockey, motorsports, golf, boxing and soccer
  • News & Weather – National, local and international coverage including NBC News Now, Fox Weather, and LiveNOW from FOX
  • Creator & Specialty Programming – Programming featuring Hot Ones, Spotify’s The Ringer, Futcrunch, Idle Mode, comedy, action sports, gaming, esports and other creator-led content.
  • Additional Programming – Discover gaming and esports, creator-led entertainment, documentaries, podcasts and other specialty programming, including eCLUTCH (exclusive) and more.

Sony, again, assured watchers that Live TV on PS5 will be refreshed with new programming, channels, and more in the future. It's all only available for the U.S. for now, but plans to bring it to Canada, as well as additional regions, are in the works.

"We hope you enjoy this new easy way to discover and watch free entertainment directly on PS5," Sony said.

Sony furthed detailed Live TV on PS5 in an FAQ section for the feature's new, official page. In case there was any confusion here, the company makes it clear: "Live TV on PS5 is completely free." There is no paid subscription, hidden fees, or downloads required, at least for now, so you should be able to log in and watch without issue soon. Both live and on-demand content will be available at launch, too.

It's proved to be an already busy week for Sony. Just hours ago, it announced plans to bring not one but two PlayStation State of Play presentations to viewers later this week. They'll take place back to back, with the first confirmed to feature another look at Final Fantasy 7 Revelation.

items.title: Ubisoft May Have Accidentally Revealed the Next Nintendo Direct Date Thanks to a Just Dance Leak
items.description: Nintendo fans believe Ubisoft may have just revealed the date of the next Nintendo Direct, and if true, it's very soon.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Nintendo fans believe Ubisoft may have just revealed the date of the next Nintendo Direct, and if true, it's very soon.

Recently, a bunch of content from the new Just Dance game, Just Dance: Decades of Hits, surfaced online, prompting a response from Ubisoft. The studio confirmed the content is real and stated that it would reveal more on September 10.

Fans have started to connect the dots that this may be the date of the next Nintendo Direct. Historically, Ubisoft shows off the dancing franchise during Nintendo Directs in September, and Nintendo tends to hold these Directs around the date mentioned in Ubisoft's post.

Hello Dancers, we are sharing an important message with you today. pic.twitter.com/Z0hFuKUVIz

— Just Dance (@justdancegame) August 27, 2026

Of course, this is just speculation, but it would track based on Nintendo's history. The company is overdue for some news on The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, and Sony is also gearing up for a State of Play later this week. It's not uncommon for the two companies to have presentations back to back like this, though that is often coincidental.

Should this come to fruition, it means we will get a Nintendo Direct next Thursday, and we'll likely hear more about it early next week. It's unclear what else might show up at the Nintendo Direct, but you can likely expect a big focus on the Ocarina of Time remake, since that releases in November. We may also get a tease of what's on the horizon for 2027, but we'll just have to wait and see.

items.title: LEGO Officially Reveals Wallace & Gromit-Themed Set
items.description: LEGO has officially revealed its first Wallace and Gromit-themed set, which depicts the iconic British duo in their vintage motorbike and sidecar.
items.author: Blythe Dujardin
items.content:
LEGO has officially revealed its first Wallace and Gromit-themed set.

The set depicts the iconic British duo in their vintage motorbike and sidecar with references to the stop-motion movies and original clay designs. The set is up for preorder on the online LEGO Store, priced at $99.99 with a release date of October 1.

The Wallace & Gromit set is the newest addition to the LEGO Ideas line, a program where fans can submit their own original set designs. After a series of fan-voting, LEGO ultimately picks some submissions to turn into official sets.

The Wallace & Gromit set was originally designed by Sébastien Esnault and submitted to the 90s Throwback - The Next Chapter challenge, where it took home the Grand Winner prize. The official LEGO version of the set looks pretty darn similar to the original build, having simply refined the faces of the iconic duo as well as the structure of the motorbike.

To accompany the set’s reveal, LEGO released an interview with the original Fan designer on their blog. Esnault felt thematically inspired by the duo’s humor and inventiveness, and explains his specific approach to building them in brick form: “To recreate the distinctive clay look, I deliberately chose the most rounded LEGO elements wherever possible.”

The official set includes 1038 pieces, mathing out to slightly over 10 cents ber brick. It’s also marked as an 18+ set intended for adults, so expect some level of complexity.

Wallace and Gromit first used this version of the motorbike and sidecar in A Close Shave, where it’s eventually revealed to have emergency flying features. The plane features don’t seem to have made the LEGO cut, but the shape, color, and license plate are all loyal to the original design.

Images on the LEGO website show off some smaller details, including goggles that Gromit can actually wear and a dedicated motorcycle that can open and close. Easter eggs inside that hatch include box of orange crackers in the style seen throughout the series as well as a diamond referencing the iconic heist from The Wrong Trousers.

The LEGO listing has videos demonstrating some poseability in the duo’s heads and arms. Designer Esnault highlights the effort put into each character’s expressions, saying “It only takes a tiny change in their angle to transform Gromit’s expression from curious to amused or worried.” It doesn't seem like you can fully separate Gromit or Wallace from their vehicle, however, so don’t expect this set to fill the void of action figures.

LEGO Ideas: Wallace & Gromit is now up for preorder and will be releasing on October 1.

Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.

items.title: Housemarque Co-Founder Ilari Kuittinen Announces Exit from Saros Developer After 31 Years
items.description: Housemarque co-founder Ilari Kuittinen has announced his exit from the PlayStation studio after 31 years.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Housemarque co-founder Ilari Kuittinen has announced his exit from the PlayStation studio after 31 years.

The Saros developer shared the news with its followers with Kuittinen's final message, confirming today as his last with the team. It's a lengthy letter to fans that saw the studio head wave goodbye after overseeing the launch of arcade-y classics like Saros, Returnal, Resogun, and more.

"After 33 years in the games industry and 31 incredible years at Housemarque—the studio I co-founded with Harri Tikkanen—today marks my last day at the company," he said. "Starting out in 1993 with Terramarque, and then joining forces with Harri to establish Housemarque in 1995, we had a passion for games but no real blueprint for building a business. Looking back, I feel immensely fortunate. We had the luck of being in the right place at the right time during three decades of incredible industry growth, allowing us to stay fiercely independent for 26 years before finding a home within the PlayStation Studios family."

"My core purpose as a leader has always been simple: to facilitate an environment where extraordinary creators have the freedom and protection to do what they do best."

Housemarque has evolved in unique ways through the years. Though its commitment to gameplay has remained through the decades, it branched beyond simple shoot-em-ups throughout the lifecycles of the PlayStation 4 and PlayStation 5 consoles.

PlayStation fans will remember when Resogun helped the PS4 launch in 2013. Twin-stick shooters like Alienation and Nex Machina would then arrive in 2016 and 2017, respectively, but Housemarque then went on to truly push the boundaries of its capabilities with its more story-driven roguelike, Returnal, for PS5 in April 2021.

Sony officially cemented the company as a PlayStation Studio later that same year, and in April of this year, it released its follow-up, Saros. Kuittinen was there for it all.

In his letter, he pointed to Housemarque's evolution into a AAA developer, its games, and its status as a pioneering Finnish game studio as three particularly noteworthy achievements he and the team have managed to accomplish. He also clarified that this isn't a sudden change; studio veteran Sami 'Haxu' Hakala took over as managing director July 1, 2026. It's something Kuittinen said he, Hakala, and the rest of the team have been carefully planning behind-the-scenes.

"Housemarque’s strategy and creative vision are in exceptional hands," he added. "As for me? After 33 continuous years without a major break, I am taking a rare and well-deserved breather trying to find out how good I am at doing nothing! To Harri, our partners at SIE, our global industry friends, and every single team member who has ever walked through Housemarque’s doors: thank you for making the past 31 years the privilege of a lifetime."

A final message from our co-founder, Ilari Kuittinen pic.twitter.com/ubf0yZJBWq

— Housemarque (@Housemarque) August 31, 2026

IGN gave Saros a 7/10 review upon its launch earlier this year. We said, at the time, that it "tries at an interesting and ambitious story it isn't always able to effectively tell, but Housemarque has once again proved that its bullet-hell sensibilities mesh incredibly well with fluid and challenging action."
